How metrics work

Each detection center is a candidate fish position. Centers within the link distance form connected groups; a chain of links can join fish farther apart. Single fish are shown separately. The random comparison places the same number of points uniformly inside the selected tank crop 399 times and compares mean nearest-neighbor distance. A low percentile means tighter spacing than those random placements in that frame; adjacent video frames are not independent tests. Inch estimates use the paper-grid calibration and are approximate. When the detected count is low, the detector checks close to the crop edge, then may split a large joined region. These estimates are marked in the raw export. Reflections can create extras, and fish are not tracked between frames. Read the full method.
